notes.title: Trope Tales Cinematic Trailer
notes.notes:
[p]We didn't want to spoil it before it happened, but we finally finished our cinematic trailer!

You can check it out in the trailers available at the top of the Trope Tales page!

Appreciate the voice acting contributions of our amazing friend: [url="https://www.instagram.com/mmoysee/"]https://www.instagram.com/mmoysee/[/url][/p][p](Let us know if anyone needs voice acting - he's awesome)[/p][p][/p][p]Now that we've finished the cinematic trailer it is back to the grindstone. We're reimagining the introduction to Einstein and reviewing everything to make sure the base is solid as we work out the next chapters. [/p][p][/p][p]For anyone that has tried the demo we're open to feedback so feel free to leave a comment letting us know what you enjoyed (or what you hated if something didn't work for you!). 

Hopefully the cinematic trailer expresses the fun, silly, and funny game we're trying to make and hope to deliver to you guys. 

Until next time!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44922177/a04594c2667058b97117f347cff58fb010e36086.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Level up: We're in the clouds, nyaa~!
notes.notes:
[p]We're super excited to announce we now support steam cloud cross platform saves! [/p][p][/p][p]Now you can start playing on one device and swap to another without losing your save![/p][p][/p][p]Steam has a neat feature where you can setup cloud saves automatically by describing the file path and file extensions you want saved to the cloud. Once configured we were able to setup the path rules for Mac too meaning your cloud saves are cross platform![/p][p][/p][p]We frequently play on Steam Deck for testing along with Mac and Windows so this felt magical to see the same save float seamlessly between platforms.[/p][p][/p][p]Our hope is to support key major platforms (Windows, Mac, Linux, Steam Deck) on launch and we hope this update will help if people are playing across multiple devices![/p][p][/p][h3]Now live in the demo!![/h3][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44922177/bd0dd7a10daf3be6fc01dfdb70abc10d23c24660.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Demo Feedback Updates
notes.notes:
[p]Based on preliminary feedback from the demo, a few changes have been made to the game:[/p][p][/p][h3]Fixed Bugs[/h3][list][*][p]The "Shell" status effect (imparted by Shell, AoE Shell, Good Touch, and Good Breath) crashed the game due to a missing effect file[/p][/*][*][p]The party and First Villain were not removed from the top of Einstein's Tower after the First Villain was defeated, meaning you could walk to the roof and battle him a second time[/p][/*][*][p]Princess would appear in Dawnstar Palace in the throne room after you finished speaking to her father and left the castle[/p][/*][*][p]Hats and Robes incorrectly claimed that they raised M.ATK, when in fact they only raised M.DEF[/p][/*][*][p]The "AoE" variants of debuff spells (AoE Blind, AoE Silence, etc) were not properly applying any debuff. These skills now work[/p][/*][*][p]The "Slow" debuff was not triggering the proper message when an enemy lost a turn[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]New Interactions[/h3][list][*][p]Every well in the game can now be entered[/p][/*][*][p]New dialogue was added to a few NPCs following key plot advancement[/p][/*][*][p]Added three new tutorials:[/p][list][*][p]If you attempt to leave a party member without talking to them, a message will inform you that party members are optional[/p][/*][*][p]When Princess joins the party, a small tutorial dialogue teaches you about the two-weapon skill system[/p][/*][*][p]When OCG joins the party, a small tutorial dialogue informs you that she is auto-battle only[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Descriptions were added to all skills and spells. These were about 40% written by me and 60% written by ChatGPT (full disclosure required as my game now contains content produced by Generative AI, which was not true before)[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Updated the damage formula[/h3][p]The previous damage formula for [u]most[/u] attacks was:[/p][code]Multiplier * (ATK - DEF)[/code][p]Distributing the "Multiplier" you can rewrite this as:[/p][code]Multiplier * ATK - Multiplier * DEF[/code][p]Looking at this in two parts, we have:[/p][list][*][p][b]Your starting damage:[/b] computed by multiplying your ATK by the skill's modifier[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mitigation:[/b] we [u]subtract[/u] some amount, computed by multiplying the enemy DEF by the same modifier[/p][/*][/list][p]This simple formula had two undesirable effects.[/p][p]First, it means that building defense [b]rapidly[/b] caused damage to fall to 0, since the value of defense gets multiplied based on the strength of the skill. So long as your defense met or exceeded the enemy attack, you were invincible. On the other end of the stick, it severely limited my ability to add defense to enemies to avoid the same effect - giving enemies even a little defense risked the player dealing zero damage to them.[/p][p]Second, it caused buffs to be unexpectedly strong against enemies who had defense. Imagine a hypothetical battle where you have 40 ATK and the enemy has 36 DEF. Using a skill with a 5x multiplier you would deal 20 damage. If Princess cast ATK UP on you, this would triple your ATK stat to 120. Now the same skill deals 420 damage! A buff intended to give a 3x multiplier just gave you a 21x multiplier, all because the enemy had defense.[/p][p]The new formula is:[/p][code]Multiplier * ATK * (ATK / (ATK + DEF))[/code][p]Now let's break this into two parts. We have:[/p][list][*][p][b]Your starting damage:[/b] computed by multiplying your ATK by the skill's modifier, same as before[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mitigation:[/b] we [u]multiply[/u] by some fraction to reduce the damage, computed as the ratio of your ATK to the enemy DEF[/p][/*][/list][p]Now if the enemy has equal DEF to your ATK, this ratio is 1:1 and you deal half damage. If the enemy has half as much DEF as you do ATK, the ratio is 2:1 and you deal 2/3 damage. Conversely if the enemy has twice as much DEF as you do ATK, the ratio is 1:2 and you deal 1/3 damage.[/p][p]This new formula solves both of our earlier issues.[/p][p]For starters, no matter how much defense the enemy has, you will always deal [u]some[/u] damage. This means I can safely add defense to enemies as a way to make them harder without increasing their total HP, and as a way to make enemies strong against either physical or magical attacks. It also means that there's reason for the player to continue stacking defense after they have exceeded the enemy's ATK value, because at no point is the player taking 0 damage from enemies.[/p][p]Next, it has solved the issue of buffs being overpowered when enemies have defense. Let's return to the hypothetical battle of 40 ATK versus 36 DEF using a skill with a 5x multiplier. Before getting buffed you will deal 105.26 damage. After getting buffed you will deal 461.54 damage. This is only a 4.38x increase, not a 21x increase! Much more reasonable.[/p][p][/p][p]Note that skills with "special" damage calculations were not impacted:[/p][list][*][p]Gravity always does 25% of the enemy's current HP, with no mitigation[/p][/*][*][p]"Cancer" skills (white magic attack skills) have lower multipliers, but bypass magic defense[/p][/*][*][p]Poison deals 5% of the enemy's max HP, with no mitigation[/p][/*][*][p]Armor Pierce bypasses physical defense[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Updated Experience Curve[/h3][p]The built-in RPG Maker experience curve has four variables you can tune:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44922177/6ee35edc872b1a93d80b347622eb6f2cdff525a7.png"][/img][/p][p]The formula for the total experience to reach a certain level is then computed as:[/p][code]Math.round(
  (base * Math.pow(level - 1, 0.9 + acc_a / 250) * level * (level + 1)) /
    (6 + Math.pow(level, 2) / 50 / acc_b) +
    (level - 1) * extra
)[/code][p]This can be written more simply as:[/p][code]numerator = (base * A * B * C)
denominator = (6 + D)

total_exp_for_level = (numerator / denominator) + "some extra"[/code][p]The "some extra" here is a very small amount (the maximum value for the "extra" parameter is 50, and the maximum level is 99, meaning this can't exceed 4900), so we can mostly ignore it when considering late game curves.[/p][p]So let's look at these A, B, C, and D values more closely:[/p][list][*][p]A = (level - 1) ^ (0.9 to 1.1) -- the exact value between 0.9 or 1.1 is chosen based on "Acceleration A"[/p][/*][*][p]B = level[/p][/*][*][p]C = level + 1[/p][/*][/list][p]For very high levels (after level 50 or so) the difference between "level - 1", "level", and "level + 1" is negligible. So we can simplify by pretending these are all just "level":[/p][list][*][p]A = level ^ (0.9 to 1.1)[/p][/*][*][p]B = level[/p][/*][*][p]C = level[/p][/*][/list][p]Since "0.9 to 1.1" is "about 1", we can simplify once more by saying that A is "approximately equal to level ^ 1"[/p][p]This means the entire numerator simplifies to:[/p][code]numerator = base * level * level * level = base * level^3[/code][p]Just like we ignored "some extra" because it was a very tiny value as numbers got large, we can similarly ignore the "6" in the denominator. So the denominator is essentially:[/p][code]denominator = level^2 / (some stuff)[/code][p]Where this "some stuff" is based on the Acceleration B value[/p][p]Some simple algebra shows us that we can simplify:[/p][code]total_exp_for_level = (base * level^3) / (level^2 / (some stuff))
                    = (base * (some stuff)) * (level^3 / level^2)
                    = (constant) * (level)[/code][p]That's a lot of math to say: as your level increases, the experience curve becomes [u]linear[/u]. In fact, if Acceleration A is less than 25, the experience to go from level 98 to 99 is [b]less than[/b] the experience to go from level 97 to 98! When Acceleration A is equal to 25 we're dealing with a linear function, and when Acceleration A is greater than 25 it's a function that grows only [u]slightly[/u] faster than linear.[/p][p][/p][p]So what does this mean for game design?[/p][p]A common expectation is that as you progress in the story, enemies will get harder and will give more experience. But if the experience curve is linear, then increasing the experience from enemies will lead to accelerated leveling! While it may take an hour of grinding in the early regions to get from level 10 to 11, it only takes 2 minutes of grinding in the last dungeon to get from level 98 to 99. Levels come so fast that they stop meaning anything.[/p][p]Given that stats grow linearly with your level and skills acquisition is (by default) based on level, this means that you will experience very little growth in power for most of the game then fly through all of your skill and stat gains right before the game is over. This is hardly as engaging as growing gradually as the story progresses.[/p][p][/p][p]After researching how large JRPGs handled experience curves (Final Fantasy, Dragon Quest, Breath of Fire, Golden Sun,...) I opted for a three-part model:[/p][list][*][p]During early levels (1 - 30 or so) I wanted the experience curve to be roughly linear. This way if you choose to grind, time spent grinding is directly rewarded proportional to time spent, but if you choose to fly through the story any "missed" experience is rapidly earned from late-game enemies.[/p][/*][*][p]During mid levels (30 - 60 or so) I wanted the experience curve to be roughly quadratic. This puts pressure on players to stop grinding and start progressing, as their gains become farther spaced apart and continued time in low-level battles becomes inefficient.[/p][/*][*][p]During late levels (60 - 90 or so) I wanted the experience curve to be roughly cubic. This way giving [u]huge[/u] experience rewards for end-game enemies will rapidly catch up under-leveled players without throwing over-level players [u][i]accidentally[/i][/u] to level 99 (reaching max level should be a conscious choice, not the result of bad experience curves).[/p][/*][/list][p]So to start, I drafted the following formula for "experience to [u]next[/u] level" (rather than "total experience to this level"):[/p][code]exp_to_next_level = A + B * L + C * L^2 + D * L^3[/code][p]This gives us:[/p][list][*][p]A constant ("base") experience to next level, "A"[/p][/*][*][p]A linear component[/p][/*][*][p]A quadratic component[/p][/*][*][p]A cubic component[/p][/*][/list][p]I then tuned A, B, C, and D such that I hit my level goals:[/p][list][*][p]At level 15 (halfway between 1 and 30), L = 15, L^2 = 225, L^3 = 3,375[/p][list][*][p]In order to keep this portion of the game linear, I needed C x L^2 and D x L^3 to both be less than 15[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]At level 45 (halfway between 30 and 60), L = 45, L^2 = 2,025, L^3 = 91,125[/p][list][*][p]In order to keep this portion of the game quadratic, I needed C x L^2 to be greater than 45, but I needed D x L^3 to be less than C x L^2 (and ideally less than 45)[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]At level 75 (halfway between 60 and 90), L = 75, L^2 = 5,625, L^3 = 421,875[/p][list][*][p]In order to keep this portion of the game cubic, I needed D x L^3 to be greater than C x L^2 which needed to be greater than 75[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]Note that the value of "A" isn't actually all that important, and only impacts the lowest of levels.[/p][p]Some example values of B, C, and D which accomplish all goals above are:[/p][list][*][p]B = 1[/p][/*][*][p]C = 1 / 30[/p][/*][*][p]D = 1 / 2000[/p][/*][/list][p]Once I had the formula for experience to next level, I applied general summation formulas to compute the total experience to a given level:[/p][code]total_exp_to_level_N = sum(1 to N, exp_to_next_level_N)
= sum(A + B*L + C*L^2 + D*L^3)
= sum(A) + sum(B*L) + sum(C*L^2) + sum(D*L^3)
= sum(A) + B*sum(L) + C*sum(L^2) + D*sum(L^3)

sum(L) = N * (N + 1) / 2
sum(L^2) = N * (N + 1) * (2 * N + 1) / 6
sum(L^3) = (N * (N + 1) / 2)^2 = sum(L)^2[/code][p][/p][p]I wrote a plugin for this new formula, being sure to incorporate the "basis", "extra", "acc_a", and "acc_b" values so that I could tune the experience curve for each character in the UI.[/p][p]Here's a table showing the difference in required experience for different levels before and after the change:[/p][p][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=",,"][tr][th][p]Level[/p][/th][th][p]Previous Exp[/p][/th][th][p]New Exp[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td][p]5[/p][/td][td][p]459[/p][/td][td][p]475[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]10[/p][/td][td][p]3,179[/p][/td][td][p]3,056[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]15[/p][/td][td][p]10,097[/p][/td][td][p]10,281[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]20[/p][/td][td][p]22,809[/p][/td][td][p]25,650[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]25[/p][/td][td][p]42,483[/p][/td][td][p]53,600[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]30[/p][/td][td][p]69,829[/p][/td][td][p]99,506[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]35[/p][/td][td][p]105,130[/p][/td][td][p]169,681[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]40[/p][/td][td][p]148,299[/p][/td][td][p]271,375[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]45[/p][/td][td][p]198,961[/p][/td][td][p]412,775[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]50[/p][/td][td][p]256,544[/p][/td][td][p]603,006[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]60[/p][/td][td][p]389,635[/p][/td][td][p]1,171,150[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]70[/p][/td][td][p]541,649[/p][/td][td][p]2,065,556[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]80[/p][/td][td][p]707,078[/p][/td][td][p]3,398,975[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]90[/p][/td][td][p]881,424[/p][/td][td][p]5,287,156[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]99[/p][/td][td][p]1,043,132[/p][/td][td][p]7,575,265[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][h3]Other[/h3][p]Following the multiple game crashes as a result of assets being missing from the final build, I opted to build my own "unused asset remover" tool.[/p][p]Over the past few weeks I've been gradually working on this program which intelligently scans your entire game database as well as plugin code to find asset references. It's very similar in nature to [url="https://starlit.itch.io/rmrm"]RPG Maker Resource Manager by Starlit[/url], with a few key differences:[/p][list][*][p]My tool runs about 200x faster (this is not an exaggeration, this was measured performance) through a combination of:[/p][list][*][p]Never processing any data file or plugin more than once (Starlit's tool will process each file [u]once per asset[/u])[/p][/*][*][p]Using the Aho-Corasick algorithm for substring detection instead of grep, which has higher performance for finding multiple possible substrings[/p][/*][*][p]Multi-threading[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]My tool can rename assets and will update all references found[/p][/*][*][p]My tool can detect duplicate assets (same file hash) and merge these duplicates[/p][/*][*][p]My tool will warn if a reference is found to an asset that doesn't exist (this actually caught a missing asset in chapter 9 of my game)[/p][/*][*][p]My tool provides a preview of assets (supports both image and audio at this time)[/p][/*][*][p]My tool has a [u]much[/u] lower false positive rate through a combination of:[/p][list][*][p]JSON parsing data files[/p][/*][*][p]Lexers for JavaScript files to extract string literals (ignores comments, variables names, etc)[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44922177/5a056edbbe0bd0d8e9d08dedcd155268bc9c420e.png"][/img][/p][p]This tool will be made available on itch.io for $9.99 once I've done a little bit more cleanup to the UI and fixed a few minor bugs.[/p][p]I also plan on releasing this tool [u]free[/u] on Steam for anyone who buys the full Trope Tales game when it's released![/p][p]The latest version of the demo utilized my tool to remove unused assets rather than RPG Maker's built-in "Remove Unused Assets" feature. This resolved the crash with the "Shell" effect, as well as prior crashes from missing front-view battle sprites which I have been manually copying over to the final release.[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Demo Patch: Crash on First Villain
notes.notes: [p][b]What Changed?[/b][/p][p]When fighting the First Villain at the end of Chapter 6, the game would crash with an error:[/p][quote][p]Failed to load: "img/enemies/Actor3_3.png"[/p][/quote][p]This file did not exist in the demo build of the game, despite existing in playtest and development builds. I've uploaded a new copy of the game with this file replaced.[/p][p][/p][p]At the same time, some less game-breaking bugs were resolved:[/p][list][*][p]The Item Shop in Dawnstar Palace no longer sells a 0-gold no-name item which does nothing[/p][/*][*][p]The Church in Fairy Falls now only opens after Einstein is defeated, rather than if you just keep knocking on the door enough[/p][/*][*][p]The Goddess in the Fairy Grotto will only appear after you have been defeated by the First Villain (Unbeatable version), rather than after you defeat Einstein[/p][/*][*][p]A 21 megabyte WAV file that accidentally slipped into the prior demo build was removed, reducing the game's size on disk accordingly[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]Root Cause[/b][/p][p]RPG Maker MZ has two different battle modes: "side view" and "front view". In Trope Tales, side view is the default for [b][i]most[/i][/b] of the game. However when fighting the Four Main Villains (and a handful of other important boss characters to come) the game switches to a front view battle. This puts the boss front-and-center with no distractions, making the battle feel a bit more epic.[/p][p]RPG Maker stores all sprites for "side view" enemies in "img/sv_enemies" and stores all "front view" enemies in "img/enemies". So if you ever intend to battle an enemy in both modes, you'll need to include their image in both of these folders.[/p][p]The problem comes in with RPG Maker's "Exclude Unused Assets" feature. This feature allows you to automatically delete any images, audio files, or animations that are never referenced in your game anywhere. Apparently if your default battle mode is "side view", RPG Maker deletes [b][i]the entire[/i][/b] "img/enemies" directory. On the contrary, if your default battle mode is "front view", RPG Maker deletes the entire "img/sv_enemies" directory.[/p][p]This means that when building my game with "Exclude Unused Assets" checked, the front view sprites were removed from the final build.[/p][p]Short-term, in order to fix this, I've built the game three times:[/p][list][*][p]Once for Windows with "Exclude Unused Assets" checked[/p][/*][*][p]Once for Mac OS with "Exclude Unused Assets" checked[/p][/*][*][p]Once for Windows with "Exclude Unused Assets" [b][i]unchecked[/i][/b][/p][/*][/list][p]This third build created a properly packed and encrypted version of the image file which I could then copy to the other two builds. I uploaded these two new builds with the missing image included.[/p][p]Long-term, I have a better fix: I've been working on an RPG Maker Asset Manager tool which can more accurately scan for used assets. It detects assets referenced in plugin configurations, assets referenced indirectly (e.g. via tags in message blocks), assets hard-coded into plugins, etc. It can even detect when you switch from front view to side view in your game, and will persist both folders. When my full game releases I intend to make this tool available on Steam as a free download for anyone who buys Trope Tales. I'll also make the tool available standalone on itch.io when it's finished.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][b]Discovery[/b][/p][p]Once again, [url="https://steamcommunity.com/id/maloktheimmortal/"]Malok[/url] gets the credit for reporting these bugs. Huge thank you![/p]

notes.title: Demo Patch: Weapons Now For Sale!
notes.notes: [p][b]What Changed?[/b][/p][p]Upon entering the Weapon Shop in Good Kingdom (the first city after you leave Arcadia) the game would enter a buggy state where it did not respond to any keyboard or mouse inputs and you could not exit the shop or interact in any way. This required crashing the game to escape.[/p][p]This bug has been patched. Now entering the Weapon Shop will not break and you can successfully purchase your first sword in Good Kingdom![/p][p][/p][p][b]Root Cause[/b][/p][p]Several events were added to various maps to create the gameplay and cinematic trailers for the game. These events would auto-move the player or various NPCs around the map to create motion and intrigue, and do so in a consistent and predictable way so we didn't risk an NPC walking off-screen during the trailer.[/p][p]One such event was added to the weapon shop to demonstrate the player walking in, walking up to the counter, and making a purchase.[/p][p]Since this was just a temporary event and not intended to be part of the final release, the event did not clean itself up or flag itself as "complete" after moving the player up to the counter. Instead, it kept running in an infinite loop to continue walking the player forward into the counter forever.[/p][p]When cleaning up the events prior to the demo release, I neglected to remove this one -- leading to the bug.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Discovery[/b][/p][p]Huge thanks to [url="https://steamcommunity.com/id/maloktheimmortal/"]Malok[/url] for discovering and reporting this bug during demo play![/p]

notes.title: Slight Demo Delay (Sorry)
notes.notes: [p]Posting a quick update about the demo release (it IS coming soon, I swear!)[/p][p][/p][p]As a new Steam developer, the thousands of options and buttons and features and actions in the Steamworks backend can be very overwhelming, and it's easy to think you've done everything right only to realize you're missing something at the last moment. This whole experience has given me an appreciation for the people who post 5-minute trash games with no content, because at least they managed to create a header capsule in the exact right pixel dimensions to be accepted by the Steam store... It's serious [b][i]work[/i][/b] to get a game visible in the store![/p][p][/p][p]I had an app for Trope Tales. This app's Steam store was approved, I had created both Windows and Mac depots, I had created test and default builds, I had configured installation info, I had set up [b][i]all[/i][/b] of the required info (system requirements, genres, tags, OS support, controller support, multiplayer support, content rating, etc)... I had Trope Tales [b][i]ready to go[/i][/b], so I could hit the "release" button at any moment. The only issue was that the story wasn't finished, so I wasn't ready to hit the release button. No worries, I thought. I'll just make a "demo" package and release that![/p][p][/p][p]So here's where I messed up:[/p][p][/p][p]A demo is [b][i]a separate app[/i][/b] from your main one! This meant I had to create a whole new (demo) app, set up a whole new collection of images, fill out the description, set up the OS support, set up controller support,... I had to set everything up again from scratch. Not that bad, though. Just took a couple of hours. But then... I had to submit it for review again.[/p][p][/p][p]So here we are... I have a demo build uploaded and ready to go, but my app is sitting in Steam review. The process can take up to 2 weeks, although I've heard it's usually done after 1. Whenever Steam review is complete, the demo will become available. Until then, I apologize for the delay![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44922177/1c3be5ea869dd1ac3b2c63509e6838289d391b60.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Demo Coming June 2025
notes.notes:
Tropes Tales [u][b]Demo[/b][/u] coming June 2025!

After much thought and consideration, and a lot of poopy diapers, I have realized that it would be ambitious to release my full vision for Trope Tales in the next three months.

While my vision is not grand, the best laid plans of mice and men often go awry.

Not wanting to release nothing and get into an endless cycle of pushing deadlines and leaving people waiting, I've decided to release [i]what I have, as I have it[/i], with more to come later.

The current plan is to release chapter 1 through 6 in June 2025 [u][b]as a free demo[/b][/u]. Then, as chapters are complete, I will update the demo with additional content. Depending on my ability to find time to work, this may mean additional chapters will already be available on the initial release date. So far the story is complete through chapter 9, but there is a lot of missing polish and other elements.

Once the last chapter (chapter 18) is complete, the demo will go offline and the full game will be made available for $4.99.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44922177/1aad19e829745e94ce0c4b8116eb6af29dfdcd88.jpg[/img]
